newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen losing steam Mon.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen losing steam Mon.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the second consecutive session and turnover was higher, but analysts said the market was likely to continue to lose steam after the 1.6-percent rise that followed Wednesday's 3.2-percent gain.

"The higher turnover is a good sign...but stocks might be mixed on Monday because the market is usually not too dynamic after a long weekend," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
Markets are closed on Friday for All Saints Day.
Other analysts said Thursday's buying after price fixing was not strong enough to signal major growth on Monday.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.6 percent to 13,497.9 points and turnover rose 29.5 percent to 115.8 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said biggest mover Espebepe surged 9.5 percent as speculators sought to take advantage of the firm's previous 45.2-percent drop on news it might go bankrupt.
Continuous trade turnover was at 2.8 million zlotys with biggest mover Animex down 6.7 percent.
NFI units rose 2.5 percent to 144 zlotys in the regular bourse session and were flat at 144 zlotys in 15.6- million-zloty continuous trade. --Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
